clue.text: Hey, this is what a conjuror must say quickly

definitions.text: Hey, this is what a conjuror must say
definitions.meaning: a magician completes a trick with the cry 'Hey ...!', so the second word of that cry is wanted
a musical tempo marking meaning very fast

explanation.surface: A magician's patter: the word said when performing a trick at speed.
explanation.definitionFit: The stage magician's catchphrase is 'hey presto', and in music the Italian tempo word means rapid.

clue.text: He who calls to order audio equipment

definitions.meaning: the presiding officer of the House of Commons calls members to order
a loudspeaker attached to a hi-fi

explanation.surface: Someone shouting 'order!' at a set of hi-fi gear.
explanation.definitionFit: The chair of a parliamentary chamber has this title, and a loudspeaker box goes by the same name.

clue.text: Furniture on which many a hand has been laid

definitions.text: Furniture on which many a hand has been laid

parts.words: Furniture on which many a hand has been laid
parts.note: a hand here is a set of playing cards laid down during a game of bridge or whist, not a palm resting on wood

explanation.surface: A piece of furniture that countless palms have rested upon.
explanation.definitionFit: A small folding table is used for games of bridge and whist, where hands of cards are put down.

clue.text: Twins for example capsized small car

indicators.note: a boat that capsizes turns over, so in this down clue the abbreviation is turned upside down

parts.note: EG is the abbreviation of exempli gratia, for example
the Mini is a famous small British car

explanation.surface: A pair of twins overturned in a little car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capsized' turns EG into GE before MINI.
explanation.definitionFit: The zodiac sign represented by Castor and Pollux, the heavenly twins.

clue.text: Deeply planted a ground cereal

parts.note: far means a long way, deeply as in far gone
something planted is in the ground

explanation.surface: Seed sown deep in the soil grows into milled grain.
explanation.definitionFit: Flour or meal made from cereal grain, used in puddings and breakfast foods.

clue.text: Ring-grip sought by mountaineer who wants a leg up

definitions.text: Ring-grip sought by mountaineer who wants a leg up

parts.words: Ring-grip sought by mountaineer who wants a leg up
parts.note: read as a hold on the lower limb in a wrestling ring, and as the secure place a climber needs to step upward

explanation.surface: A climber searching for something to grab as they ask for a boost.
explanation.definitionFit: A climber's secure step on rock, and also a wrestler's grasp of an opponent's lower leg.

clue.text: Sound room for secretion

indicators.note: sound tells us the clue word is to be taken by how it is pronounced, not spelt

parts.note: a chamber in a house, pronounced the same as the watery discharge

explanation.surface: A soundproof chamber set aside for a gland's discharge.
explanation.definitionFit: A thin watery discharge from the eyes or nose.

clue.text: White notes Brown scaling Russian mounts

indicators.note: scaling means climbing, so in a down clue the colour word is read upward

parts.note: tan is a light brown colour
the Urals are the mountain range dividing European and Asian Russia

explanation.surface: A man named Brown climbing in the Russian mountains, with snowy scenery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scaling' turns TAN into NAT. On a piano the white keys play the plain notes, neither sharp nor flat.
explanation.definitionFit: Notes that are neither sharp nor flat, played on the piano's white keys.

clue.text: Watch the gossip

definitions.meaning: a pocket watch that strikes the hours again when a spring is pressed
someone who passes on what they hear to others

explanation.surface: Keep an eye on the local chatterbox.
explanation.definitionFit: A chiming timepiece with a striking mechanism, and a person who tells everyone what was said to them.

clue.text: The best policy produces silvery leaves in the garden

definitions.meaning: the proverb says truthfulness is the best policy
the plant Lunaria, grown for its translucent silver seed pods

explanation.surface: A proverb about good conduct paired with a pretty garden plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Truthfulness, per the old proverb, and a garden plant whose papery seed discs gleam like silver coins.

clue.text: Like a lady stiffly corsetted, or could one say stayed?

indicators.note: asks whether the word could be spoken in place of another that sounds identical

parts.note: fitted with stays, the bones of a corset, and pronounced like the word for prim

explanation.surface: A woman laced tightly into her corset, described with a pun.
explanation.walkthrough: Stays are the whalebone strips in a corset, so a lady in one is 'stayed', and also prim and stiff.
explanation.definitionFit: Sedate and prim in manner, as stiff as someone laced into a corset.

clue.text: A dark horse which troubles no day-dreamer

definitions.text: A dark horse which troubles no day-dreamer

parts.words: A dark horse which troubles no day-dreamer
parts.note: read as a female horse of the dark hours, which only bothers those asleep at night

explanation.surface: An unexpected racing contender that bothers no idle fantasist.
explanation.definitionFit: A frightening dream comes only during sleep, so it never disturbs someone daydreaming.

clue.text: Glacial material found up in, and also at foot of precipice

indicators.note: the foot of a down entry's word is its end, so take the closing letters of the clue word

explanation.surface: Frozen matter discovered high on a cliff and at its base.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at foot of' takes the closing letters of 'precipice'. 'found up in' is a second route: ECI sits inside the word and reads upward as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Glaciers are made of frozen water.

clue.text: Far too grand for a mince pie actor

indicators.note: to mince is to chop finely, so these letters are cut up and rearranged

explanation.surface: An overblown performer for a Christmas pie.
explanation.definitionFit: Overly dramatic and theatrical, like grand opera.

clue.text: Beautiful appeal very abbreviated in famous portrait artist

indicators.note: in places the appeal and the abbreviation inside the artist's name

parts.note: Sir Peter Lely, court portrait painter to Charles II
O is the exclamation of appeal, as in 'O Lord'
V is the short form of very

explanation.surface: Praise of a lovely painting by a celebrated portraitist.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: attractive and pleasing to look at.

clue.text: Eccentric member of society

definitions.meaning: an odd chap, a strange man
a member of the ..., a British friendly society for mutual aid

explanation.surface: An eccentric person who belongs to a club.
explanation.definitionFit: A strange person, and a member of a mutual-benefit friendly society in Britain.

clue.text: Criminal who runs a bankrupt business

definitions.meaning: a fence, who handles stolen goods
an official appointed to manage an insolvent firm's affairs

explanation.surface: A crook in charge of a failed company.
explanation.definitionFit: A handler of stolen goods, and the court-appointed administrator of an insolvent firm.

clue.text: Tiny electronic bulb went first

definitions.meaning: a light-emitting diode
past tense of to lead, to be at the front

explanation.surface: A small light that was at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: A light-emitting diode, and the past tense of heading a procession.

clue.text: Description of spirits, anaesthetic and ale concoction

parts.note: ether was an early anaesthetic

indicators.note: a concoction mixes ingredients, so these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Words describing a cocktail of knockout gas and beer.
explanation.definitionFit: Ghosts are insubstantial and airy, beings of another world.

clue.text: To sum up, it was just half way through the first millenium

parts.note: AD, Anno Domini, marks the years of the Christian era from its first millennium onward
halfway through a thousand years is the year 500, and D is the Roman numeral for 500

explanation.surface: A summary of history: it was exactly halfway through the first thousand years.
explanation.walkthrough: The midpoint of the first millennium is AD 500, written with the Roman numeral D.
explanation.definitionFit: To total figures, to calculate a sum.

clue.text: Black necklace and ear-rings for the old yuppies

parts.note: jet is a glossy black stone, and jet-black means very black
matching jewellery pieces sold together form a set

explanation.surface: Black jewellery worn by fashionable young professionals of the past.
explanation.definitionFit: The rich, fashionable people who flew between glamorous resorts, a forerunner of young upwardly mobile professionals.

clue.text: Passed bill on the theatre's bill board?

definitions.meaning: a bill passed by parliament becomes law
each turn on a theatre programme or poster

explanation.surface: Legislation listed among the turns on a playhouse poster.
explanation.definitionFit: A statute made law by parliament, and one turn in a variety show's line-up.

clue.text: Looked for meals wheels on wheels?

definitions.text: Looked for meals wheels on wheels?

parts.words: Looked for meals wheels on wheels?
parts.note: read as searched for food, and as a description of the meals-on-wheels service, which delivers food to elderly people

explanation.surface: Searching for a hot dinner delivered by van.
explanation.walkthrough: Meals on wheels delivers hot meals to the elderly, so it is food 'for aged' people. The repeated 'wheels' may be a misprint.
explanation.definitionFit: Searched about for food, as animals do, and split in two gives a phrase meaning intended for the elderly.

clue.text: A bit of leg gives nothing but youthful infatuation

parts.note: the calf is the back of the lower leg
love means a score of zero in tennis

explanation.surface: Flashing some leg brings only teenage romance.
explanation.definitionFit: A short-lived adolescent crush on someone.

clue.text: Enquiring how a monarch rules

definitions.meaning: putting a question, questioning
a monarch rules in the role of king, split as two words

explanation.surface: Asking about the way a sovereign governs.
explanation.definitionFit: Putting a question to someone, and, split in two, the capacity in which a male sovereign reigns.

clue.text: All that is left for housing development

definitions.meaning: a dead person's property, everything left in a will
a planned group of houses built together

explanation.surface: An inheritance handed over to build new homes.
explanation.definitionFit: A deceased person's total assets, and a planned area of homes built together.

clue.text: Accommodation for camping campanologists

parts.note: campanologists are bell-ringers, so their shelters under canvas would suit their hobby

explanation.surface: Lodgings for bell-ringers on a camping holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: Conical tents with a central pole, shaped like a bell, which suit bell-ringers on holiday.

clue.text: Cruel misappropriation of profit

indicators.note: misappropriation is wrongful use, so the letters are put to a different use in a new order

explanation.surface: Ill-gotten money taken by embezzling cruelly.
explanation.definitionFit: Money or gain, especially when sought greedily ('filthy lucre').

clue.text: Smallest amount of stale crumble

indicators.note: stale bread crumbles into bits, so these letters fall into a new order

explanation.surface: A tiny portion of a dry, crumbling cake.
explanation.definitionFit: The minimum quantity, the tiniest portion.

clue.text: Organised vice Heath drove out

indicators.note: organised means arranged, so the letters are arranged afresh

parts.note: Edward 'Ted' Heath was a British Conservative prime minister

explanation.surface: A politician expelled organised crime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Organised' rearranges VICE into EVIC. TED is Edward Heath, UK prime minister 1970-74.
explanation.definitionFit: Forced out of a home or premises, as a landlord expels a tenant.

clue.text: Rude suggestion as to where Newport visitors should bathe

parts.note: a word naming a location, the preposition in
Newport is the main town on the Isle of Wight, beside the Solent strait, where visitors swim

explanation.surface: Advice on where holidaymakers in an island town should go swimming.
explanation.walkthrough: The Solent is the strait between the Isle of Wight and mainland England; Newport is the island's county town.
explanation.definitionFit: Impertinent and disrespectful in speech or behaviour.

clue.text: French preposition in oral test

indicators.note: in places the French word inside the other clue word

parts.note: de is French for of or from

explanation.surface: A French grammar question in a spoken exam.
explanation.definitionFit: A severe trial or painful experience.
